claims.claim: A CMAJ study released Monday finds daily cannabis use is more common than daily alcohol use among Canadian adults and equals or exceeds daily cigarette use among people younger than 35.
claims.episode_span: daily cannabis use is more common than daily alcohol use among Canadian adults
claims.source_title: Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: Daily cannabis use is more common than alcohol among Canadian adults, and it is equal to or exceeds daily cigarette use among those younger than 35, says a new study in The Canadian Medical Association Journal.

claims.claim: The study used the 2023-2024 Canadian Community Health Survey of nearly 100,000 people age 18 and older.
claims.episode_span: nearly 100,000 people age 18 and older
claims.source_title: Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: It involved nearly 100,000 respondents to the 2023-2024 Canadian Community Health Survey, a nationally representative survey of individuals age 18 and older.

claims.claim: Among men aged 25 to 34, daily cannabis use was 10.8 percent, daily alcohol 2.9 percent and daily cigarettes 8 percent.
claims.episode_span: daily cannabis use was 10.8 percent, against 2.9 percent for daily alcohol and 8 percent for cigarettes
claims.source_title: Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: Researchers found daily cannabis use was the highest among males aged 25 to 34 years at 10.8 per cent, exceeding both daily alcohol use at 2.9 per cent and cigarette use at 8 per cent.

claims.claim: Among women aged 25 to 34, daily cannabis use was 6.8 percent, daily alcohol 1.2 percent and daily cigarettes 4.5 percent.
claims.episode_span: among women in that age group the figures were 6.8 percent, 1.2 percent and 4.5 percent
claims.source_title: Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: A similar pattern was observed among females aged 25 to 34 years, for whom daily cannabis use 6.8 per cent, exceeding daily alcohol use at 1.2 per cent and to a lesser extent, daily cigarette use at 4.5 per cent, according to the study.

claims.claim: Among women 18 to 24, daily cannabis use was 6.6 percent, daily alcohol 0.4 percent and daily cigarettes 2 percent.
claims.episode_span: daily cannabis use was 6.6 percent, daily alcohol 0.4 percent and daily cigarettes 2 percent
claims.source_title: Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: For females in this age bracket, daily cannabis use, at 6.6 per cent, was markedly higher than alcohol use at 0.4 per cent. Cigarette use was 2 per cent, with similar patterns observed among male respondents.

claims.claim: Three in five daily cannabis users reported no concurrent daily cigarette use, nine in ten reported no concurrent daily alcohol use, and 68 percent of daily users smoke cannabis.
claims.episode_span: three in five reported no concurrent daily cigarette use, nine in ten reported no concurrent daily alcohol use, and 68 percent of daily users smoke cannabis
claims.source_title: Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: The research found that three in five who use cannabis daily did not report concurrent daily cigarette use and that nine in 10 did not report concurrent daily alcohol use.
